To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mixing characteristics of gas and liquid phases in bubble columns are strongly influenced by the height to diameter ratio and the column scale.
the gas phase mixing time is proportional to the column height and the liquid phase mixing time is a function of the column height and diameter.
the mixing characteristics of gas and liquid phase in bubble column reactors can be investigated from the virtual tracer experiments coupled with the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method to study mixing characteristics of large scale reactors.
the study of the mixing characteristics of gas and liquid phases in a bubble column reactor using a virtual tracer method coupled with computational fluid dynamics simulation.
the development of a new approach to the design of a bubble column reactor based on the use of the dispersion coefficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gas phase mixing is better in the lower part of the column, while the liquid phase mixing is better at the upper part.
the virtual tracer method is a useful tool in investigating mixing characteristics in bubble columns, especially for large scale reactors.

the mixing pattern in bubble column reactors is not only a function of column geometry, but also a function of the gas holdup, and the superficial gas velocity, and this is true in the range of column diameter from 0.14 to 0.90m.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mixing characteristics in large bubble columns are similar to those in small columns, but with a scale effect, and that the mixing time is not affected by height/diameter ratio.
a large scale bubble column reactor can be well simulated by a virtual tracer experiment and the results are consistent with the experimental measurements.
the gas phase mixing is more intense in the upper part of the column and less intense in the lower part of the column.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dispersion coefficients and mixing times for the gas and liquid phases are comparable.
the dispersion coefficient is a strong function of the height of the reactor.
the mixing time of the gas and the liquid phases are similar and the scale effect is significant for the gas phase.
